claims.text: Everyone must choose whether they'd rather risk rejection now or guarantee regret later. Winners fear regret; losers fear rejection.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Failure is literally a prerequisite for success. Greatness rejects all first-time applicants.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Starting a business requires the same number of rejections as a job search. Getting hired involved multiple interviews, job applications, and resumes—one sale in an employee context. Business operates identically; the only variable is whether you can tolerate years of regret if you don't try.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: job search context vs. business context
claims.mechanism: Both require handling repeated rejection; the decision framework differs by time horizon (immediate career vs. years of regret).

claims.text: Champions consistently win because they hate losing more than they love winning, and they expect to win due to preparation level relative to competitors. Most people lose because they are excited about winning, which paradoxically prevents them from achieving first place.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Intrinsic motivation from fear of loss and preparation-based confidence compounds; extrinsic motivation (excitement about winning) reduces focus and preparation.

examples.text: A job applicant applies to one company, gets rejected, and concludes they cannot get a job. This illustrates survivorship bias: applying once, experiencing one rejection, and generalizing it as failure.

Alex Hormozi has completed a 10-stage roadmap from zero to $100M+ revenue multiple times across software, physical products, service businesses, and brick-and-mortar, validating that the stages and constraints apply across business models.

practices.text: Risk rejection now rather than guarantee regret later.
Handle the level of rejection in business the same way you handle job search rejection.
Focus on preparation and competitive advantage relative to others, not on the excitement of winning.
